Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

epidemia 1.0.0.9001

Installs with current versions of Stan again, adds new model options and fixes several bugs. The new options are off by default, so models that do not use them are the same as in 1.0.0.

Installation

  • Installs with current rstan, StanHeaders and rstantools (checked with rstan 2.32.7, StanHeaders 2.39.1 and rstantools 2.7.1): the Stan programs use the array syntax required since Stan 2.33, the sparse matrix helper csr_matrix_times_vector2() compiles against the Stan Math types of Stan >= 2.26, and the build files follow rstantools 2.7 (C++17). rstan and StanHeaders >= 2.26 are now required (#67).
  • Sources and help pages are ASCII, so installation no longer fails in non-UTF-8 locales (#65).
  • The unused inst/include/tests.cpp, which included a missing header, is removed (#61).
  • R CMD check runs on GitHub Actions, with --as-cran on Linux, macOS and Windows, and on Linux also with R-devel and the previous R release.

New features

  • epiinf(): gen can hold a generation distribution for each group, as a named list or a matrix with named columns. They are matched to groups by name, or through the new gen_group argument.
  • epiinf(): importations = TRUE adds a constant number of imported infections each day in each group to the renewal equation, with prior prior_importations (half-normal with scale 0.2 by default). Off by default (#15).
  • epiobs(): period models observations that are totals over the period days ending on their date, such as weekly counts with period = 7. Daily observations (period = 1) remain the default.
  • discretize_cdf() turns a continuous delay distribution, given by its CDF, into the probability mass function on whole days used by gen and i2o (#3).
  • Cases and deaths can be fitted together, with deaths fully reported at a known case fatality ratio (CFR) and cases at an unknown reporting rate in each group: epiobs(deaths ~ 0 + offset(cfr), link = "identity") fixes the ascertainment of deaths at the CFR held in column cfr, and epiobs(cases ~ 0 + group, link = "logit") estimates a reporting rate for each group. The epiobs() help page now describes this.
  • New article “Weekly Counts, Importations and Counterfactuals”, including counterfactuals with newdata and a joint fit of weekly cases and deaths with the deaths averted.
  • epiobs(aux_by_group = TRUE) gives each group its own auxiliary parameter, such as its own negative binomial dispersion, for any observation type that has one: cases and deaths alike. Each group’s parameter has the type’s prior_aux, on the scale that prior_aux_on sets, and is named by group (cases|reciprocal dispersion[north]). Several groups no longer need one observation model each (at most 10 are allowed). With the default, FALSE, the model is that of 1.0.0: a test checks that its log density and gradient equal 1.0.0’s, and another that a fit recovers different dispersions in two groups of simulated data. The weekly-counterfactuals article has an example.
  • epiobs(prior_aux_on = "inv_sqrt") makes prior_aux a prior on one over the square root of the auxiliary parameter: prior_aux = rstanarm::normal(0, 1) then gives the negative binomial’s 1/sqrt(phi) a half-normal(0, 1) prior. The help page now says that a normal prior with location m is m + s|z|, so the default keeps phi >= 10.
  • epirt(prior_covariance = rstanarm::normal(0, s)) gives the standard deviation of each random effects term a half-normal(0, s) prior instead of decov’s, when every term has one coefficient, as in (0 + x || group).
  • lognormal(meanlog, sdlog) is a new prior for epiinf(prior_seeds = ): the log of each group’s daily seeded infections is normal, with a mean (and standard deviation) per group if given, so seeds can be centred on each group’s early counts.
  • The rw() help page explains that rows with an NA time have no walk term, so a walk can start in the second period, with the first period’s log Rt given by the intercept alone.
  • rw(noncentred = TRUE) samples a walk’s steps as standard normal variables and multiplies them by the walk’s scale. The model is the same, but it samples much better when the scale is near zero. The reported steps are the scaled ones either way, so posterior_rt() and the other posterior simulations are unchanged.

Bug fixes

  • posterior_predict() returned NULL for models with several observation types unless a single type was asked for. It now returns a list named by type, so one counterfactual gives, for example, both cases and deaths.
  • posterior_predict() drew log-normal observations on the wrong scale (meanlog = mu - sigma^2 / 2 instead of log(mu) - sigma^2 / 2).
  • The error for random effects in an observation formula no longer ends in “FALSE”.
  • R|Sigma[...] reported the Cholesky factors of the random effects’ covariance matrices, not the covariances its name says: epim() converted them in a helper and dropped the result. For a term with one coefficient it was the standard deviation rather than the variance.
  • Log-normal observation models with zero observations failed to start, with rstan’s unhelpful “no more scalars to read”. Zeros have zero density under the log-normal, so epim() now stops early and says to set them to NA or use another family.

Other changes

  • plot_rt() no longer plots the seeding period, where Rt does not enter the model; seeding = TRUE restores it (#54).
  • Posterior simulations (posterior_rt(), posterior_predict() and the plots) no longer print sampler timings.
  • check_time_as_date() rejects numeric date columns again on R >= 4.3.
  • The check that gen sums to one allows rounding error up to 1e-8, as Stan’s simplex check does.
  • A broken link in the model description vignette is fixed (pull request #63).
  • findbars(), nobars() and subbars() now come from reformulas, where lme4 2.0 says they have moved.
  • R CMD check --as-cran notes are cleared: class tests use inherits(), S3 methods are registered and match their generics, and a help link names its package.
  • The pkgdown workflow builds the site with the current pkgdown and R on Linux. It checks the site on pull requests and deploys it on pushes to master, as before.

epidemia 1.0.02021-10-25

  • First version submitted to CRAN
  • Bug fixed for latent infections and first Rt with pop_adjust
  • reorganized files to correctly attribute copyright.
  • New model for adding vaccination adjustments
  • latent infections switched to normal, from log-normal
  • Additional vignettes and model description
  • Additional noise options for infection process
  • Significantly more flexible modeling of seeding process
  • Many small bug fixes

epidemia 0.7.0

  • Changes to general interface - new epiinf() function for representing infection model
  • Improved package website, with better description of the model and examples in the vignettes.
  • Ability to model latent infections explicitly - replacing renewal equation
  • Removed ‘pop’ and replaced with column of susceptibles in dataframe. This allows susceptible population to reduce over time due to vaccinations.
  • Improved error checking in epim(), with more informative messages
  • scaled_logit for epiobs
  • Full integration with Bayesplot package, and a plot.epimodel method which easily allows the user to choose different components of the model.
  • Fixed bug which meant “fullrank” was actually using “meanfield”
  • Ability to use random walks in the epiobs models
  • Choose between identity, scaled logit, and log link for epirt
  • Plot the (potentially transformed) linear predictors for both epiobs and epirt
  • Additional families for epiobs - normal and lognormal
  • Add summary method and printing for epimodel objects
  • Plots improved, allowing step for plot_rt, and improved formatting

epidemia 0.6.0

  • Substantial changes to interface: Added epirt and epiobs objects
  • Different and more flexible observation models
  • Improved structure to epimodel objects
  • Refactoring of main epim function
  • Improved plots, including interactive plots using plotly
  • Forecast evaluation using coverage and different metrics
  • Ability to do an initial run fit to cumulatives within epim
  • Updated tests, documentation and vignettes

epidemia 0.5.3

  • Improved model description in introduction vignette

epidemia 0.5.2

  • Passes R CMD Check with no warnings
  • Updated installation instructions

epidemia 0.5.1

  • Renamed stan files to avoid errors with Rstan 2.12.
  • Plotting vignette

epidemia 0.5.0

  • Random walk terms parsed separately as input to stan files. Variance parameter sampled in stan, and so can make predictions.
  • pseudo-log scales for plot_infections and plot_observations
  • control over date range for all plots
  • option to plot smoothed Rt in plot_rt

epidemia 0.4.0

  • Features for counterfactual analysis and predictions

epidemia 0.3.3

  • Added vignette describing priors
  • Description of collinearity issues in ‘resolving problems’ vignette
  • Form for potential beta testers

epidemia 0.3.2

  • Citation file
  • Fixes to documentation in website

epidemia 0.3.1

  • Website fixes
  • Separate index for website and github

epidemia 0.3.0

  • Website and more extensive vignettes

epidemia 0.2.0
